title: Read and write under the same monitor

blocks.text: The page's `WrongMonitor` writes under `writeLock` and reads under `readLock`. Both methods are `synchronized`, yet there is no happens-before between them: an unlock is only seen by a later lock **of the same monitor**. The fix, `SameMonitor`, uses one lock for both.
Write `SharedCell`, an `int` cell shared between threads. Every method locks **the cell itself** (`this`), so a caller can make several calls one atomic step by holding the cell's monitor:

items: `addAndGet(int delta)` adds `delta` and returns the new value, as one step.

rows: another thread holds `synchronized (cell)` while you call `get()`

cases.says: set, get and addAndGet keep one int value, and a caller holding the cell's monitor can make several calls one atomic step.
get() takes the cell's own monitor, the one set() releases, so it waits while another thread holds it.
set() takes the cell's own monitor, so it waits while another thread holds it.
addAndGet() reads and writes under the cell's own monitor, so the compound update waits while another thread holds it.

origin.section: 5. Forgetting that synchronized visibility applies only to the same monitor

concepts: synchronized gives visibility only between threads that lock the same monitor, so readers and writers must share one lock.
synchronized gives both mutual exclusion and visibility, which a compound update of shared state needs.
